Background knowledge

Source: R/knowledge.R
knowledge.Rd

Background knowledge about a causal graph: required and forbidden edges, tiers and exogenous nodes.

Usage

knowledge(..., nodes = NULL)

Arguments

...

Statements, as above, or bare node names.

nodes

Character vector of node names. If given, the knowledge is about exactly these nodes: no statement, and no later edit, may name another.

Value

A caugi_knowledge object.

Details

Statements:

  • A %-->% B: the edge A --> B is required.

  • !(A %-->% B): the edge A --> B is forbidden. The parentheses are required, and ! applies to each edge inside them.

  • tier(t1 = A + B, t2 = C, max_lag = NULL): edges between tiers point from the earlier tier to the later one, and nodes in tiers more than max_lag apart are not adjacent. Nodes without a tier are not constrained by it.

  • exogenous(A, B): no edge points into A or B.

Edges are written as in caugi(), so A + B %-->% C and A %-->% B %-->% C work too.

See also

Other knowledge: is_knowledge(), orient(), required(), set_tiers(), tiers()

Examples

bk <- knowledge(
  tier(baseline = A + B, followup = C + D),
  A %-->% C,
  !(B %-->% D),
  exogenous(A)
)
bk
#> <knowledge; nodes: A, B, C, D>
#>   tier(baseline = A + B, followup = C + D)
#>   exogenous(A)
#>   A %-->% C
#>   !(B %-->% D)
edges(bk, expand = TRUE)
plot(bk)
